questions.question: How many sandstone Doric columns support the floor above the Capitol Crypt?
questions.explanation: Forty Aquia Creek sandstone columns support the Rotunda's floor.

questions.question: Why is the room beneath the Capitol Rotunda called the Crypt?
questions.explanation: Its vaulted design resembles crypts used beneath churches; no one is buried there.

questions.question: What does the white star at the center of the Capitol Crypt's floor mark?
questions.explanation: The central compass stone marks Washington's division into NW, NE, SW and SE.

questions.question: How many people have been buried inside the U.S. Capitol?
questions.explanation: Congress once considered placing George and Martha Washington there, but both remain at Mount Vernon.

questions.question: Approximately how many rooms are inside the U.S. Capitol?
questions.explanation: The Architect of the Capitol counts approximately 540 rooms in the building.

questions.question: On what date did Congress first meet in the U.S. Capitol building?
questions.explanation: Congress first met in the building on November 17, 1800.

questions.question: How many windows are in the Capitol's dome?
questions.explanation: The Architect of the Capitol identifies 108 windows in the dome.

questions.question: Who designed the Capitol's current cast-iron dome?
questions.explanation: Thomas U. Walter designed the dome built between 1856 and 1866.

questions.question: What happened to construction of the Capitol dome during the Civil War?
questions.explanation: Dome construction continued despite the outbreak of the Civil War; other extensions paused.

questions.question: What famous fresco is painted inside the Capitol dome?
questions.explanation: Constantino Brumidi's Apotheosis of Washington rises above the Rotunda floor.

questions.question: How many stars circle the helmet of the Capitol's Statue of Freedom?
questions.explanation: The statue's helmet is circled by nine stars.

questions.question: What unusual material tips protective points on the Statue of Freedom?
questions.explanation: Ten bronze points tipped with platinum protect parts of the statue from lightning.

questions.question: What is on the front of the Statue of Freedom's shield?
questions.explanation: Freedom holds a shield with thirteen stripes representing the original colonies.

questions.question: What was removed from an early Statue of Freedom design after Jefferson Davis objected?
questions.explanation: A liberty cap associated with emancipated slaves was removed after Jefferson Davis objected.

questions.question: How many major sections were used to cast the Statue of Freedom?
questions.explanation: The bronze Statue of Freedom was cast in five main sections.

questions.question: What do wheat wreaths on the World War II Memorial's columns symbolize?
questions.explanation: Wheat represents agriculture and oak represents industrial strength.

questions.question: What do oak wreaths on World War II Memorial columns represent?
questions.explanation: Oak represents industrial contribution to the war effort.

questions.question: How many bronze bas-relief panels flank the World War II Memorial entrance?
questions.explanation: Twenty-four panels chronicle America's wartime service and home front.

questions.question: What are the World War II Memorial's two victory pavilions called?
questions.explanation: They commemorate the two major theaters of the war.

questions.question: About how many individual stones make up the World War II Memorial?
questions.explanation: The NPS estimates nearly 17,000 individual stones.

questions.question: When was the World War II Memorial formally dedicated?
questions.explanation: It was formally dedicated Memorial Day weekend in 2004.

questions.question: Which detail shows how the memorial honors U.S. home-front work?
questions.explanation: The wheat and oak wreaths acknowledge agriculture and industry as vital to the war effort.

questions.question: How tall are the Lincoln Memorial's exterior columns?
questions.explanation: The NPS measures the 36 exterior columns at 44 feet tall.

questions.question: How many stone 'drums' form each of the Lincoln Memorial's exterior columns?
questions.explanation: Each exterior column is composed of twelve individual sections, called drums.

questions.question: What is written above the Lincoln Memorial's colonnade?
questions.explanation: Names of 36 states and their Union admission dates appear on the exterior frieze.

questions.question: What year was the Lincoln Memorial dedicated?
questions.explanation: The memorial was dedicated on May 30, 1922.

questions.question: Which architect designed the Lincoln Memorial?
questions.explanation: Henry Bacon designed its temple-like structure; Daniel Chester French sculpted Lincoln.

questions.question: How heavy is the seated Lincoln statue?
questions.explanation: The 28-piece white Georgia marble statue weighs about 175 tons.

questions.question: How tall is the seated Lincoln figure from head to foot?
questions.explanation: The figure itself is 19 feet tall; a standing Lincoln at the same scale would be 28 feet tall.

questions.question: What two major Lincoln speeches are carved inside the memorial?
questions.explanation: The interior inscriptions feature the Gettysburg Address and the Second Inaugural Address.

questions.question: Which way do the Vietnam Memorial's V-shaped walls point?
questions.explanation: One arm points toward the Lincoln Memorial and the other toward the Washington Monument.

questions.question: Which symbol beside a Vietnam Wall name denotes someone still missing in action?
questions.explanation: A cross indicates MIA; a diamond indicates confirmed death.

questions.question: How long did the initial Vietnam Wall dedication include a reading of names?
questions.explanation: A 56-hour reading accompanied the memorial's 1982 dedication.

questions.question: What year was the Vietnam Veterans Memorial Wall dedicated?
questions.explanation: The memorial was dedicated in November 1982.

questions.question: What is the name of the competition-winning Vietnam Memorial designer?
questions.explanation: Maya Lin was a 21-year-old Yale architecture student when her design won.

questions.question: How many Ionic columns form the Jefferson Memorial's circular colonnade?
questions.explanation: The memorial's circular colonnade has 26 Ionic columns.

questions.question: What type of marble forms much of the Jefferson Memorial's exterior?
questions.explanation: The memorial uses white Imperial Danby marble quarried in Vermont.

questions.question: Which president dedicated the Jefferson Memorial in 1943?
questions.explanation: Franklin D. Roosevelt presided over the April 13, 1943 dedication.

questions.question: The Jefferson Memorial was dedicated on what occasion?
options: The end of World War II
questions.explanation: Its dedication fell on the 200th anniversary of Jefferson's birth.

questions.question: Who designed the Jefferson Memorial?
questions.explanation: John Russell Pope was selected to design the memorial in 1935.

questions.question: Which part of the Jefferson Memorial was replaced in bronze in 1947?
questions.explanation: A bronze Jefferson statue replaced a wartime plaster figure in 1947.

questions.question: In 1799, how many enslaved people at Mount Vernon were legally owned by George Washington himself?
questions.explanation: Mount Vernon's research distinguishes 123 people owned by George Washington from others owned by the Custis estate or other owners.

questions.question: Washington's Mount Vernon gristmill had how many pairs of millstones?
questions.explanation: One pair ground corn into meal, while a second ground wheat for high-quality flour.

questions.question: What was the approximate peak annual whiskey output of Washington's distillery?
questions.explanation: The distillery produced about 11,000 gallons in 1799.

questions.question: How many enslaved workers helped distill whiskey at Mount Vernon?
questions.explanation: Mount Vernon's research names six enslaved distillers: Hanson, Peter, Nat, Daniel, James, and Timothy.

questions.question: How many stills did Washington's distillery use at peak production?
questions.explanation: The distillery operated five stills and a boiler at peak production.

questions.question: What beverage did Washington's 1790s distillery make most often?
questions.explanation: Its principal output was rye whiskey made with rye, corn and malted barley.

questions.question: Was Washington's whiskey typically stored for years in charred barrels?
options: No, it was generally sold unaged
questions.explanation: At the time, whiskey was typically sent to market in uncharred barrels without aging.

questions.question: Where did George Washington request to be buried in his final will?
questions.explanation: Although congressional leaders considered placing Washington's remains at the Capitol, his will specified burial at Mount Vernon.

questions.question: Who was the first military service member buried at Arlington in 1864?
questions.explanation: Private William Christman was buried on May 13, 1864.

questions.question: How many acres did Arlington encompass when designated a military cemetery in 1864?
questions.explanation: Two hundred acres were formally designated for the military cemetery.

questions.question: What community existed on Arlington land during and after the Civil War?
questions.explanation: Freedman's Village served formerly enslaved people and included homes, schools and churches.

questions.question: In what year did Freedman's Village at Arlington finally close?
questions.explanation: The federal government closed Freedman's Village in 1900.

questions.question: Which two U.S. presidents are buried at Arlington National Cemetery?
questions.explanation: William Howard Taft (1930) and John F. Kennedy (1963) are buried there.

questions.question: How did Sergeant Edward Younger select the World War I Unknown Soldier in France?
options: Placing white roses on a casket
questions.explanation: He placed a spray of white roses on one of four unidentified soldiers' caskets.

questions.question: Which ship brought the World War I Unknown Soldier's casket from France?
questions.explanation: The USS Olympia transported the casket to Washington in 1921.

questions.question: What year was the large marble sarcophagus added to the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier?
questions.explanation: The original tomb was a simple slab; its sarcophagus was installed in 1932.

questions.question: Which regiment has guarded the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier since 1948?
questions.explanation: The 3rd U.S. Infantry Regiment, known as the Old Guard, took over the ceremony in 1948.

questions.question: Who was the first U.S. president buried at Arlington?
questions.explanation: William Howard Taft was buried at Arlington in 1930.

questions.question: Roughly how long is the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool?
questions.explanation: The pool stretches 2,028 feet between the Lincoln Memorial and the World War II Memorial.

questions.question: Approximately how much water can the Lincoln Reflecting Pool hold?
questions.explanation: The NPS estimates almost 6,750,000 gallons.

questions.question: On what holiday was the Washington Monument cornerstone laid in 1848?
questions.explanation: Its cornerstone was laid July 4, 1848.

questions.question: What happened at Washington Monument grounds during the Civil War?
options: The monument served as a prison
questions.explanation: The unfinished monument grounds were used as a government cattle depot.

questions.question: When was the Washington Monument capstone put in place?
questions.explanation: The capstone and aluminum tip were installed December 6, 1884.

questions.question: In what year was the Korean War Veterans Memorial dedicated?
questions.explanation: It was dedicated July 27, 1995, the 42nd anniversary of the armistice.

questions.question: In what year was the memorial's additional remembrance wall unveiled?
questions.explanation: The newer Wall of Remembrance was added in 2022.

questions.question: What phrase appears at the Korean War Veterans Memorial?
options: Ask Not What Your Country Can Do
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Freedom Is Not Free' is inscribed at the memorial.
